name: Low Sun
tagline: A vermilion broadsheet whose masthead casts the real shadow of the sun over Oslo.
summary: The page is the colour of the Nordic sun sitting on the horizon, and the name Albretsen fills the first screen like a masthead, casting a long shadow computed from the actual sun over Oslo. Below it every product plays on a live musical score, and the masthead's variable weight thickens when the products are busy. It reads like a serious publication with a sense of humour: proof of taste, delivered as telemetry.
voice: Warm, witty and exact, like a good newspaper column. Example: "Busier days get bolder type; quiet ones get a lighter touch."
motion: Nothing moves unless something happened: a real event pulses one letter and tears a thin slice of the masthead for a tenth of a second, then everything settles.
sound: An opt-in music box: each event plucks the pentatonic pitch of its row on the score, a deploy plays a soft chord, a glitch ticks.
mark: An abstract low sun: a disc above a horizon line with its long shadow below, reused as the status glyph (up, rising, on the horizon, set).
